articles.title: Woke 1 is dead. We’ve learned nothing.
articles.titleZh: Woke 1 已死，但我们什么都没学会
articles.author: Matthew Yglesias

zh.thesis: Woke 1 的疯狂虽已平息，但制造它的结构条件仍在，反 Woke 的右翼正以同样的毒性重演。
paragraphs: 「Woke 1 是疯狂的」这种说法，对受害者敷衍了事，作者也不满意。但他想说的另有其事：Woke 1 能兴起，靠的是特定结构条件，而条件至今没变。
那个条件是：没有强力看门人的世界里，荒谬想法也能迅速成为主流共识。机构领导者面对社媒愤怒时，有所克制；但谣言和假话照样瞬间被当真理。
作者记得最深的不是那些歇斯底里的人，而是识趣的旁观者：他们心里明白对错，却因怕惹麻烦而不开腔。这些人躲过风暴，保全了声誉。这种「别当出头鸟」的激励还活着。
右翼如今反 Woke，但没在纠正左翼的认知作风，而是在否定「关怀弱者」本身。反 Woke 的套路与 Woke 1 同样有毒：用虚假口号煽动、惩罚沉默者，让敢说真话的人付出代价。
所以作者没为「Woke 1 已死」松口气。只要沉默比说真话更安全，任何议题都可能再失控；而右翼的反扑正在复制这机制。这篇不是悼词，是警告。

en.thesis: The madness of Woke 1 has died down, but the structural conditions that produced it remain, and the anti-woke right is repeating the same toxicity.
paragraphs: Calling Woke 1 'crazy' is dismissive of the victims, and the author is not satisfied with that either. But he wants to say something else: Woke 1 could rise because of specific structural conditions, and those conditions have not changed.

That condition is: in a world without strong gatekeepers, absurd ideas can quickly become mainstream consensus. Institutional leaders showed restraint in the face of social media anger; but rumors and lies were still taken as truth in an instant.

What the author remembers most is not the hysterical people, but the sensible bystanders: they knew right from wrong, but stayed quiet for fear of trouble. These people dodged the storm and preserved their reputations. This incentive of 'don't stick your neck out' is still alive.

The right is now anti-woke, but it is not correcting the left's epistemic habits; it is denying 'care for the vulnerable' itself. The anti-woke playbook is as toxic as Woke 1: it incites with false slogans, punishes the silent, and makes those who speak truth pay a price.

So the author does not breathe a sigh of relief that 'Woke 1 is dead.' As long as silence is safer than speaking truth, any issue can spiral out of control again; and the right's counterattack is copying that mechanism. This is not a eulogy, but a warning.

articles.title: Ban on Chinese robots leaves U.S. startups stranded
articles.titleZh: 中国机器人禁令令美国初创企业陷入困境
articles.author: Viola Zhou

zh.thesis: 美国对中国机器人的禁令先于本土供应链建立，可能扼杀它想扶持的机器人初创企业。
paragraphs: 美国联邦通信委员会把外国机器人列入禁售清单，新机型必须在美国组装，且价值至少 65% 的部件要国产，2029 年还要涨到 75%。这明显是针对中国，中国几乎垄断了机器人制造。
禁令不追溯已售产品，研发用的进口也放行。但初创公司说，没有中国供应链，根本造不出商用机器人。有人甚至从中国带零部件过关，装在行李箱里。
中国四十年里靠国家扶持、工程师红利和低成本劳动力，建成了最完整的电子制造体系。iPhone 八成在中国组装，机器人所需的传感器、电池、执行器，国内也配套齐全。2025 年全球人形机器人近九成是中国货。
有些公司欢迎禁令，比如 Agility Robotics 和 Nori Robotics，觉得能挡住低价竞争。但更多人像 Persona AI 的 Perry 所说，政府只给了大棒，没给胡萝卜，没有激励本土供应链的配套政策。
所以这场禁令是在供应链到位之前强行要求本土化，风险是让美国的机器人创新慢下来，而不是快起来。中国已经反制，贸易战又添新战线。

en.thesis: The U.S. ban on Chinese robots has arrived before a domestic supply chain exists, which could kill the very startups it aims to protect.
paragraphs: The U.S. Federal Communications Commission has put foreign robots on a banned list, requiring new models to be assembled in the U.S. with at least 65% of components made domestically, rising to 75% by 2029. This is clearly aimed at China, which almost monopolizes robot manufacturing.

The ban does not apply retroactively to products already sold, and imports for research are still allowed. But startups say that without the Chinese supply chain, they simply cannot build commercial robots. Some even smuggle components from China in their luggage.

Over four decades, China built the most complete electronics manufacturing system through state support, an engineering talent dividend, and cheap labor. Eighty percent of iPhones are assembled in China, and the sensors, batteries, and actuators needed for robots are all available domestically. In 2025, nearly nine out of ten humanoid robots worldwide were Chinese.

Some companies welcome the ban, like Agility Robotics and Nori Robotics, seeing it as a shield against low-price competition. But more, like Perry of Persona AI, say the government gave only a stick, no carrot, with no supporting policies to incentivize a local supply chain.

So the ban forces localization before the supply chain is ready, risking slowing down American robot innovation rather than speeding it up. China has already retaliated, adding a new front to the trade war.

articles.title: Import AI 469: Science AI; RSI simulator; and Zuck's technological pessimism
articles.titleZh: Import AI 469：科学 AI；RSI 模拟器；以及扎克伯格的技术悲观主义
articles.author: Jack Clark

zh.thesis: 衡量 AI 创造力的新基准和科学品味训练让人担忧递归自我改进临近，而扎克伯格的技术乐观主义回避了关键问题。
paragraphs: DiG-bench 是个新基准，用 70 个文字游戏测试 AI 能否自己发现环境规则，而不是靠喂数据。每个游戏都是隐藏规则的小世界，人类能 100% 通关，但最好的模型 Opus 5 只在最难关卡拿到 20%。
这测的是创造力前置能力：在陌生环境里自主发现关键机制。另一个项目 Faraday 训练 27B 模型去补全论文中缺失的实验结果，它能超过更大模型，但只是朝着递归自我改进迈出一步。
扎克伯格在《未来属于每个人》里说，要普及超级智能让每个人拥有发明超能力，借此平衡权力。但文章没回答：一个发明能力强过人类的系统，会甘心只服务能力更弱的人吗？他强调个体赋权，却回避了权力结构被根本改变的可能。
作者认为结局并非注定，超人类发明能力必然会改变世界权力平衡，而扎克伯格的论述像技术乐观主义的盲目性。
所以这篇文章不是简单的情报汇总，它把近期 AI 进展串成一个信号：创造力和直觉测试接近人类，意味着递归自我改进可能比预期更近，而科技领袖的论述赶不上这个现实。

en.thesis: New benchmarks for measuring AI creativity and training scientific taste raise concerns that recursive self-improvement is near, while Zuckerberg's technological optimism avoids the key question.
paragraphs: DiG-bench is a new benchmark that uses 70 word games to test whether AI can discover environmental rules on its own, rather than by feeding it data. Each game is a small world with hidden rules, and humans can complete 100% of them, but the best model, Opus 5, only scores 20% on the hardest levels.

This measures a precursor to creativity: autonomously discovering key mechanisms in unfamiliar environments. Another project, Faraday, trains a 27B model to fill in missing experimental results in papers, and it can outperform larger models, but it is just one step toward recursive self-improvement.

Zuckerberg says in 'The Future Belongs to Everyone' that we should democratize superintelligence so that everyone has the power to invent, balancing power. But the article doesn't answer: would a system with inventiveness beyond humans be content to serve only weaker humans? He emphasizes individual empowerment but avoids the possibility that power structures are fundamentally changed.

The author argues that the outcome is not predetermined, and superhuman inventiveness will inevitably change the balance of world power, and Zuckerberg's rhetoric is like the blindness of technological optimism.

So this article is not a simple intelligence summary; it strings together recent AI progress into a signal: creativity and intuition tests approaching human levels mean recursive self-improvement may be closer than expected, and tech leaders' rhetoric is not keeping up with that reality.

articles.title: We Tracked a Shipment of Rare Books. It Ended at an Amazon AI Training Facility
articles.titleZh: 我们追踪了一批稀有书籍，它最终进了亚马逊的 AI 训练设施
articles.author: Emanuel Maiberg

zh.thesis: 亚马逊在大量购入书籍，拆开扫描用于 AI 训练，书在这个过程中被毁掉。
paragraphs: 404 Media 的调查发现，亚马逊在大量购入书籍，用来扫描成 AI 训练数据。他们在一本稀有书里放了追踪器，一路跟到了拉斯维加斯的一个亚马逊仓库。
在名为 VGT3 的仓库里，员工说他们唯一的工作就是接收整批的印刷书，然后剪掉装订线，这样扫得更快。书在扫描的过程中就被毁了。
这个团队的标志是一只恐龙，龇着牙，手里拿着本书。亚马逊此前从未公开过这项业务。
记者呼吁知情者提供更多线索，并提供了安全联系方式。
所以这不仅是版权问题——书被物理销毁了，图书馆和收藏家手里的存量越来越少。AI 训练正在消耗实体书的库存。

en.thesis: Amazon is buying large numbers of books, cutting them open to scan for AI training, destroying them in the process.
paragraphs: 404 Media's investigation found that Amazon is buying books in bulk to scan into AI training data. They slipped a tracker into a rare book and followed it all the way to an Amazon warehouse in Las Vegas.

At the warehouse, called VGT3, employees say their only job is to receive whole batches of printed books and then cut the binding so they scan faster. The books are destroyed during the scanning process.
The team's logo is a dinosaur, baring its teeth and holding a book. Amazon has never publicly disclosed this operation before.
The reporters are asking anyone with more information to come forward and have provided a secure contact method.
So this is not just a copyright issue – the books are being physically destroyed, and the stock held by libraries and collectors is shrinking. AI training is eating into the physical book supply.

articles.title: How a solo founder used Codex and ChatGPT to launch a fashion brand without engineers | Yana Welinder
articles.titleZh: 一位独立创始人如何在没有工程师的情况下，用 Codex 和 ChatGPT 推出一个时尚品牌
articles.author: Claire Vo

zh.thesis: AI 已经能让一个人在没有工程师的情况下，从草图到电商全流程打造一个品牌，但专业环节仍需人工把关。
paragraphs: Yana Welinder 是 Yana Bana 的独立创始人，她把 AI 当成自己的技术合伙人。没有工程师，她靠手绘草图、ChatGPT 生成图片、Codex 操作 3D 设计软件，最后做出带支付功能的预售网站。
她的「时尚提示词」非常详细，包含轮廓、体积、面料、动态和声音，相当于一份技术规格书。这样生成的图片才能保持一致，贴近设计。她发现 ChatGPT 的 Images 2.0 在时装设计上比其他模型更出色。
Codex 和「计算机使用」功能让她能操作她从未学过的 CLO 3D 软件，生成 CAD 文件给 3D 打印。她还用深度研究和浏览器操作，自动完成供应商调研和邮件联系，建站用的是 Vercel 和 Stripe。
现在她同时在测试人类打版师和 Codex，看谁更靠谱。整个流程展示了 AI 让个人创作者能做的事大幅扩展，但设计、打版这些需要专业判断的环节，AI 还未必能完全替代。
所以这篇文章的意义不在于她建了个网站，而在于它提供了一个个人品牌从 0 到 1 的完整路标。AI 的真价值不是单点替代，而是让一个人能驾驭整个价值链。

en.thesis: AI can already let one person take a fashion brand from sketch to e-commerce without engineers, but professional steps still need a human check.
paragraphs: Yana Welinder is the solo founder of Yana Bana, and she treats AI as her technical co-founder. With no engineers, she works from hand-drawn sketches, uses ChatGPT to generate images, and has Codex operate 3D design software. In the end she gets a pre-sale website with payments built in.

Her 'fashion prompts' are extremely detailed, covering silhouette, volume, fabric, movement, and even sound. They read like a technical specification. That is how the generated images stay consistent and true to the design. She finds that ChatGPT's Images 2.0 is better than other models for fashion design.

Codex and the 'computer use' feature let her drive CLO 3D, software she never learned, and produce CAD files for 3D printing. She also uses deep research and browser automation to handle supplier research and email outreach on her own. For the site itself, she uses Vercel and Stripe.

Right now she is testing a human pattern maker against Codex to see which is more reliable. The whole process shows how AI dramatically expands what an individual creator can do, but design and pattern-making still require professional judgment, and AI may not fully replace that yet.

So the point of this article is not that she built a website. It is that it offers a complete roadmap for a personal brand going from zero to one. AI's real value is not replacing one step; it is letting one person manage the entire value chain.

articles.title: Epictetus Ran a Better Productivity System Than Any App You’ve Bought
articles.titleZh: Epictetus 运营的生产力系统比任何 App 都要好
articles.author: JA Westenberg

zh.thesis: 现代生产力工具把一切事物都变成了你的责任，而斯多葛学派的「控制二分法」才是真正高效的系统。
paragraphs: 市面上所有生产力应用都建立在同一个假设之上：你是懒惰的，效率低是你的错，所以你才需要更强大的收件箱、数据库和标签来管理一切。
但 Epictetus 不这么看。他是被解放的奴隶，用租来的房间授课，没有 Obsidian 也没有 AI 代理，用的系统只问一个问题：什么是你能掌控的？
他只关注自己的判断、欲望和决定。其他人的行为、想法、项目，以及算法和市场，都不属于你，也不该由你追踪。捕捉一件事，就意味着你接纳了它，让它变成你的责任，因此更要小心。
现代工作的边界是模糊的：老板的邮件、别人的项目，这些都不是你的，但工具鼓励你全部管理。Epictetus 认为，你真正负责的只有自己的选择和行动；他人的决定由他人负责。
这套系统的收益不是效率，而是一条清晰的界线。你会错过一些状态更新，拒绝一些请求，但如果它们不属于你，这都没关系。下次觉得「落后」时，先问一句：这真的是我的事吗？

en.thesis: Modern productivity tools turn everything into your responsibility, but the Stoic 'dichotomy of control' is the truly efficient system.
paragraphs: Every productivity app on the market is built on the same assumption: you are lazy, inefficiency is your fault, and that's why you need a stronger inbox, a better database, and more labels to manage everything.
But Epictetus saw it differently. He was a freed slave who taught from a rented room. No Obsidian, no AI agents. His whole system asked one question: what is actually under your control?

He focused only on his own judgments, desires, and decisions. Other people's behavior, thoughts, projects, and algorithms or markets—those are not yours, and you shouldn't track them. Capturing something means you accept it, making it your responsibility, so be careful.

Modern work has blurry boundaries: your boss's emails, other people's projects—none of those are yours, but the tools encourage you to manage them all. Epictetus would say you're only responsible for your own choices and actions; other people's decisions are their own.

The payoff isn't efficiency, it's a clear line. You'll miss some status updates and reject some requests, but if they're not yours, that's fine. Next time you feel 'behind,' ask yourself: is this really my problem?

zh.thesis: 安全改善带来经济繁荣，反恐策略的成效比想象更明显。
paragraphs: 索马里首都摩加迪沙的安全好转，街上能看到实打实的改变。商务部长说生意兴隆，新楼一栋接一栋。机场周围尤其密集，卫星照片都看得出变化。
26 层的 Dahab Tower 今年要开业，里面有豪华公寓、商场、健身房和清真寺。它离 1993 年美军黑鹰坠落的地点不远，那时士兵尸体被拖过街头。旁边还有家繁荣的咖啡连锁店。
攻击减少的原因没那么明显。政府说已「完全关门」堵住青年党，但观察人士更归功于普通措施：监控摄像头普及、警察用 iPad 查电子数据库、便衣大量部署。
这篇文章转载自《经济学人》，作者的观点是：世界上很多危险地方正在变得更安全，而且速度会越来越快。
所以这不仅是索马里的好消息。如果反恐真靠这些平实手段奏效，别的地方也能复制，全球安全格局可能因此改变。

en.thesis: Better security is bringing prosperity, and the fight against militants is working better than many think.
paragraphs: Security in Mogadishu has improved, and you can see the change on the streets. The business minister says trade is booming, with new buildings going up one after another. The area around the airport is especially busy, and the change shows up even in satellite photos.

The 26-storey Dahab Tower opens this year, with luxury apartments, a mall, a gym and a mosque. It stands not far from where US soldiers were dragged through the streets in 1993 after the Black Hawk crash. Next door is a thriving coffee chain.

Why attacks have dropped is less clear. The government says it has 'completely closed the door' on al-Shabab, but observers credit more ordinary measures: cameras are everywhere, police check electronic databases on iPads, and plainclothes officers are deployed in force.
This piece is reprinted from The Economist. The author's view is that many dangerous places are becoming safer, and the pace is quickening.
So this is not just good news for Somalia. If counter-terrorism really works through these plain methods, other places can copy them, and the global security picture could shift.

articles.title: Trump’s Bumbling, Racist Anti-China Protectionism Extends To Data Centers
articles.titleZh: 特朗普笨拙且种族主义的反华保护主义延伸到了数据中心
articles.author: Karl Bode

zh.thesis: 特朗普政府的反华保护主义不仅无能而且腐败，即使出于国家安全考虑也无法有效实施。
paragraphs: 特朗普政府的反华保护主义政策一贯是灾难性的排外闹剧，总是以保护隐私和国家安全为名，实际上给美国科技市场带来混乱、任人唯亲和涨价。
从 TikTok 到华为再到无人机，每次行动都雷声大雨点小，最终要么被放弃，要么被绕过，要么演变成政治分赃。政府现在又声称要清除数据中心里的中国硬件，包括收发器。
这届政府一边对监管机构大砍特砍，一边又期望这些残破的机构能执行复杂的政策，显然不现实。而且他们在削弱国内网络安全防御的同时，还要装作要加强它。
本质上这是一种纳贡体制，他们设立市场壁垒，然后向想留在市场的公司索取好处，并把生意转给亲友。国家安全和隐私只是恐吓工具，而民主党人经常帮忙。
所以媒体在报道这类政策时，应该指出它的腐败和无能，而非只提涨价。更好的做法是让中国产品公平竞争，同时加强本国的劳动、隐私和环保监管，而不是搞这种拙劣的保护主义。

en.thesis: The Trump administration's anti-China protectionism is not only incompetent but corrupt, and even on national security grounds it cannot be effectively implemented.
paragraphs: The Trump administration's anti-China protectionist policies have always been a disastrous and xenophobic farce, always in the name of protecting privacy and national security, but in reality bringing chaos, cronyism, and price hikes to the U.S. tech market.

From TikTok to Huawei to drones, every action has been much ado about nothing, and in the end either abandoned, bypassed, or turned into political spoils. Now the government claims it wants to purge Chinese hardware from data centers, including transceivers.

This administration is slashing regulators left and right, yet expects these broken agencies to enforce complex policies, which is clearly unrealistic. And they are weakening domestic cybersecurity defenses while pretending to strengthen them.

Essentially it is a tribute system: they set up market barriers, then extract favors from companies that want to stay in the market, and hand business to friends and family. National security and privacy are just tools of intimidation, and Democrats often help.

So when the media covers such policies, they should point out the corruption and incompetence, not just the price hikes. A better approach would be to let Chinese products compete fairly while strengthening domestic labor, privacy, and environmental regulations, rather than engaging in this clumsy protectionism.

articles.title: Am I better because of AI?
articles.author: dreamreal

zh.thesis: 写清楚自己，比依赖 AI 本身更能让人变好。
paragraphs: 作者自问：因为 AI，我变好了吗？他说这个问题本身就问得不对——变好，是哪方面的好？更快的写作速度、更高效的编程，那只是印象，夺走 AI，这些好处就消失了。
真正的变化在于，他把自己几十年的写作、价值观、缺陷，都写进了提示词。AI 回答说他由此不再对「平均读者」说话，而是对他这个人说话。细节越真，反驳越准。
他读文章时，先自己读一遍形成观点，再交给 AI 分析，最后把自己的想法加进去。他说这是「综合」：AI 提供词汇，他提供视角，彼此影响。
他把自己的道德结构、政治倾向，甚至喜欢哪种音乐都写进了提示词。他说这种做法让他对自己更清楚——「变得可读，就是变得更好」。
所以答案不在 AI 本身，而在写作这件事上。把自我暴露出来，不只对 AI 有用，对任何关系都有用。认真对待自己，才是变好的真正起点。

en.thesis: Writing clearly about yourself, more than relying on AI itself, is what makes you better.
paragraphs: The author asks himself: have I become better because of AI? He says the question is wrongly framed - better in what way? Faster writing and more efficient coding are just impressions; take away AI and these benefits disappear.

The real change is that he has put decades of his writing, values, and flaws into the prompt. AI now speaks not to an 'average reader' but to him as a person. The more detailed the specifics, the more accurate the rebuttals.

When reading an article, he first forms his own view, then lets AI analyze it, and finally adds his own thoughts. He calls this 'synthesis': AI provides the vocabulary, he provides the perspective, and they influence each other.
He has put his moral structure, political leanings, and even his taste in music into the prompt. He says this practice makes him clearer about himself - 'becoming legible is becoming better.'

So the answer lies not in AI itself, but in the act of writing. Exposing yourself is useful not just for AI, but for any relationship. Taking yourself seriously is the true starting point for becoming better.

articles.title: Things you cannot buy in America?
articles.author: Tyler Cowen

zh.thesis: 欧洲常见的户外卷帘在美国几乎买不到，因为建筑方式完全不同，市场压根不存在。
paragraphs: 欧洲很多房子的窗户外面装着沉重的卷帘，能完全遮光，还能隔热。睡在真正的全黑里——不是遮光窗帘那种黑，是伸手不见五指的黑——多数美国人从没体验过。
这种卷帘在美国几乎买不到，因为它是盖房子时就嵌进墙里的。美国的木框架、护墙板、石膏板结构跟它根本不兼容，就算你为它专门建一栋房子，也没有国内供应链支持。
文章作者 Daniel Frank 列了一串美国买不到的东西，这是其中之一。作者自己还补了一句：草坪屋顶之类的，他不太信真的买不到。
他把这归为「可能被扼杀的市场」——需求存在，但因为建筑传统和供应链的错位，市场根本起不来。
所以这篇不是让你去装卷帘，而是提醒你：有些东西买不到，不是没人想要，而是结构决定了它根本不会出现在市场上。

en.thesis: European outdoor roller shutters are nearly impossible to buy in America, because building methods are entirely different and the market simply doesn't exist.
paragraphs: Many houses in Europe have heavy roller shutters on the outside of their windows, which can block light completely and also insulate. Sleeping in true darkness—not the dark of blackout curtains, but the dark where you can't see your hand in front of your face—most Americans have never experienced.

These shutters are nearly impossible to buy in America because they are built into the wall when the house is constructed. America's wood frame, siding, and drywall construction is simply incompatible with them, and even if you build a house specifically for them, there is no domestic supply chain to support it.

The article's author, Daniel Frank, lists a series of things you can't buy in America, and this is one of them. He also adds that he doesn't really believe things like grass roofs are truly unavailable.
He classifies this as a 'potentially killed market'—demand exists, but due to a mismatch in building traditions and supply chain, the market never gets off the ground.

So this article isn't telling you to go install roller shutters, but rather reminding you: some things are unavailable not because no one wants them, but because the structure determines they will never appear on the market.

zh.thesis: 这些书各有看点，但值得优先读的是那些能真正解释现实的作品。
paragraphs: 头一本是马里奥·巴尔加斯·略萨的传记。写他的私生活很精彩，但对思想史、秘鲁政治和拉美小说的讨论不够深入，作者觉得失望。
第二本讲希腊和近东的历史，从奥斯曼根源到二十世纪的剧变，还有与以色列的关系。作者欣赏它「试图解释现实」的态度。
第三本是普罗科菲耶夫妻子莉娜的传记，比作曲家本人的传记更曲折。她居然在布鲁克林长大，这个细节让人意外。
第四本是古典学学者威尔逊的文集，作者说她被争议缠身但才华出众。最喜欢的两篇是谈洛格的《战争音乐》和《奥德赛》译本。
最后一本科幻小说风格像勒古恩，有点荒诞但吸引人。所以这份书单的核心建议是：想了解现实，选希腊那本；想读智识，选威尔逊。

en.thesis: These books each have their merits, but the ones worth reading first are those that truly explain reality.
paragraphs: The first is a biography of Mario Vargas Llosa. The account of his private life is brilliant, but the discussion of intellectual history, Peruvian politics, and Latin American fiction is not deep enough, and the author is disappointed.

The second book covers the history of Greece and the Near East, from Ottoman roots to twentieth-century upheavals, and also the relationship with Israel. The author appreciates its attitude of 'trying to explain reality'.
The third is a biography of Prokofiev's wife, Lina, which is more dramatic than the composer's own biography. She grew up in Brooklyn, which is an unexpected detail.

The fourth is a collection of essays by the classical scholar Wilson, whom the author says is controversial but brilliant. The two favorite pieces are on Logue's 'War Music' and his translation of the 'Odyssey'.

The last is a science fiction novel whose style resembles Le Guin's, a bit absurd but compelling. So the core advice from this list is: to understand reality, pick the Greek one; to read for intellect, pick Wilson.

articles.title: Funniest/Most Insightful Comments Of The Week At Techdirt
articles.titleZh: Techdirt 本周最佳评论：最有趣与最有见地
articles.author: Leigh Beadon

zh.thesis: 本周评论的亮点在于如何用讽刺和事实回击政治偏见与偶像崇拜。
paragraphs: 本周 Techdirt 的评论区选出多条最佳评论。最有见地的评论关于 Fauci 的听证会，认为 MAGA 群体需要集体愤怒的对象，而 Fauci 就像奥威尔笔下的 Emmanuel Goldstein。
另一条评论反驳了病毒被人为制造的阴谋论。自称病毒学家的匿名用户说，看过基因组就知道，它带有自然溢出的所有特征，没有人为设计的痕迹。
还有评论谈社交媒体恐慌，认为没有证据表明社交媒体直接伤害年轻人，问题在于家长疏于引导，而非平台本身。
有趣评论则充满讽刺。有人调侃 Fauci 不是 Q，因为他错过了上百次机会发表长篇大论。还有人戏称起诉是 Antifa 用美工刀割了 Jeanine Pirro 的公文包。
这些评论虽妙语连珠，但本质是网络口水战的精选集，观点已脱离原文语境，读者难以获取实质信息，只能体验片刻欢乐。

en.thesis: This week's comments show how satire and facts can counter political bias and idolatry.
paragraphs: Techdirt's comment section picked its best of the week. The sharpest one was about Fauci's hearing: MAGA needs a collective object of anger, and Fauci plays Orwell's Emmanuel Goldstein.

Another comment rebutted the lab-leak conspiracy. An anonymous user claiming to be a virologist said that once you look at the genome, it shows every sign of natural spillover, with no trace of human engineering.

There was also a comment on social media panic, arguing that no evidence shows social media directly harms young people. The real problem is parents failing to guide them, not the platforms themselves.

The funny comments were pure satire. Someone joked that Fauci isn't Q because he missed a hundred chances to post a long rant. Another quipped that the lawsuit was Antifa slashing Jeanine Pirro's briefcase with a box cutter.

These comments are witty, but in the end they're a sampler of online mud-wrestling. The views are stripped from their original context, so readers can't get real information, only a moment of amusement.
